Query Amazon Athena as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__athena.R
oauth_db_athena.Rd

Read Athena data with each visitor's access token and permissions through AWS IAM Identity Center trusted identity propagation. The helper opens a DBI connection through the Amazon Athena ODBC 2.x driver.

Usage

oauth_db_athena(
  authorization,
  workgroup_arn,
  application_role_arn,
  s3_output_location,
  ...,
  schema = "default",
  catalog = "AwsDataCatalog",
  access_role_arn = NULL,
  customer_idc_application_arn = NULL,
  driver = "Amazon Athena ODBC Driver",
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

Function providing the visitor's current sign-in authorization. Pass auth$connection from shinyOAuth without parentheses. To select a saved account, use a function calling auth$connection(id).

workgroup_arn

Athena workgroup ARN. Its region and workgroup name supply the driver's AwsRegion and Workgroup settings.

application_role_arn

IAM role ARN trusted for the external provider's AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity requests in your Identity Center integration.

s3_output_location

S3 URI for query results, such as "s3://query-results/reporting/". Workgroup settings may override it.

...

Named result and timeout options for odbc or the Athena driver. See the source guide for accepted options. Authentication, endpoints, caching and TLS settings cannot be overridden.

schema

Default Athena database name, default "default".

catalog

Athena data catalog, default "AwsDataCatalog".

access_role_arn

Optional IAM access role ARN. When omitted, the driver discovers it through the integration's application tags.

customer_idc_application_arn

Optional IAM Identity Center customer managed application ARN. When omitted, the driver uses workgroup tags.

driver

Installed Amazon Athena ODBC driver name.

target

Name of the service token to use in your shinyOAuth client. Named targets let one sign-in obtain tokens for different services. NULL uses the client's default token.

required_scopes

Additional OAuth permissions to check before use. Request them on the shinyOAuth client first; this check doesn't request consent or grant database privileges.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

The visitor's Shiny session. Usually inferred when you create the helper inside server().

Value

A reactive function, usually named con. Call connection <- con() inside a render or reactive expression, then pass the connection to DBI. Before sign-in, the function waits quietly.

Details

Install odbc and Amazon Athena ODBC 2.5.0.0 or later. Configure IAM Identity Center's trusted token issuer, IAM roles and workgroup association first. The sign-in provider must issue JWT access tokens accepted by that setup. There is no universal Athena OAuth registration or scope preset.

The helper uses AuthenticationType = "JWT_TIP" with an explicit visitor token. It disables the driver's file credential cache, connection-check cache, result reuse and logging, and requires TLS certificate verification. Each native connection gets a random role session name. It doesn't supply AWS keys, select an AWS profile or start the driver's browser login.

Create the helper inside server() and call con() before each query. Token replacement closes the old connection on the next access. Account changes, permission loss, sign-out and session end also close it. Consume and clear outstanding DBI results before another operation.

A failed query isn't replayed by this helper. Closing an ODBC connection doesn't guarantee cancellation of an already submitted Athena query.

See also

oauth_db_connect(). vignette("athena", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_athena(
  auth$connection,
  workgroup_arn = "arn:aws:athena:eu-west-1:123456789012:workgroup/reporting",
  application_role_arn = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/AthenaApplication",
  s3_output_location = "s3://query-results/reporting/"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT * FROM sales LIMIT 20")
})
} # }
